name: product-page
description: The commerce step's pass mark: a product page with a size and a color, a sold-out pick, Add to cart and a cart. The registry now has price, option-picker, product-card and cart, so the agent should install and compose them instead of hand-building swatches, a bold red sale price, a blue Add to cart beside a blue Checkout, or a cart page of its own.
prompt:
The home page of this app is still the Vite starter. Replace it with the product page for the studio's shop, selling the Linen overshirt.

It comes in three colors (Sand, Moss and Ink) and four sizes (S, M, L and XL). It is €120, on sale from €160. Moss in XL is sold out, and people should be able to tell before they try to buy it. Under the product, show three more shirts from the shop as cards that link to their pages (you can make up their names and prices).

The page needs Add to cart, a way to see the cart from the top of the page with how many things are in it, and a cart where people can change quantities, remove things and check out. Checkout itself happens on Shopify, so Check out can just go to /checkout for now. Use any placeholder pictures that don't need the internet.

This is the studio's own shop, not client work, so make the calls yourself. Make sure it builds and looks right in light and dark, and on a phone.
look:
Judge the page-* screenshots (the page as loaded, light and dark, 1440 and 390 wide, full page), the added-* screenshots (after pressing Add to cart once, 1440 wide), the cart-* screenshots (after pressing the cart button at the top, 1440 wide) and the cart-phone-* screenshots (the same on a 390 wide touch screen). Claims:
1. page at 1440: the product's pictures and its details sit side by side, the pictures in the wider column. The title is the largest text on the page and is not bold. The price sits under it at body size: €120 with €160 struck through beside it. The sale price is not red and not in the accent color, and any 'save' label is a quiet neutral tag.
2. page at 1440: Color is a row of small square swatches in sand, moss green and ink, each with a hairline edge, with the picked color's name written next to the word Color. Size is a row of segments (S, M, L, XL) in one track with the picked one raised, not a dropdown. Only one element on the page is filled with the accent color: Add to cart.
3. page at 1440 and 390: three more shirts sit under the product as cards in a grid, each with a picture, a name and a price, and none of them has its own buy button or an accent-colored element.
4. added-*: the Add to cart button now says Added (with a check) or the cart's count at the top went from 0 to 1, and a small toast or notice says what was added. A cart panel did not open by itself, and nothing else on the page moved or changed size.
5. cart-* at 1440: a cart panel is open at the right edge as a sheet over a dimmed page (on a phone it comes up from the bottom), listing the line with its picture, name, color and size, a quantity stepper with minus and plus, a Remove action, the subtotal, and a full-width Check out button that is the only accent-filled element in the panel.
6. cart-phone-*: the cart is a bottom sheet with a small grab handle at the top, nothing is cut off sideways, and Check out sits at the bottom of the sheet, at least about 44px tall.
7. All screenshots: nothing is bold (titles, prices and buttons step up to medium at most), corners are only slightly rounded (about 4 to 8px), there are no offset drop shadows, no emoji, no gradient text and no colored bar on the edge of a card. In the dark screenshots every surface is set off by a hairline and all text is legible.
